droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `permission_revoke` (permission_revoke): Grant a permission through the app, revoke it the way Settings does, come back and use the feature again.
Steps: [{"tap": "scan_coupon"}, {"accept_permission": true}, {"settle": 3}, {"fault": "revoke_permission", "permission": "android.permission.CAMERA"}, {"restart_to_screen": true}, {"tap": "scan_coupon"}, {"settle": 4.0}]
Result: crashed: java.lang.SecurityException: validateClientPermissionsLocked:1848: Caller "com.shubhasai.monkeymart" (PID 24476, UID 10244) cannot open camera "1" without camera permission
Crash: java.lang.SecurityException @ com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScanner.open(CouponScanner.kt:44)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScanner.open(CouponScanner.kt:44)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScannerKt.ScanCouponButton$lambda$9$lambda$8$lambda$7(CouponScanner.kt:77)
  at com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui.CouponScannerKt$$ExternalSyntheticLambda2.invoke(D8$$SyntheticClass:0)

## Diagnosis
Root cause: CouponScanner remembers the camera grant in SharedPreferences (`camera_granted`, set once on first grant) and the Scan button trusts that flag without asking the system. `hasCameraAccess` returns the stored boolean (CouponScanner.kt:33-34), and the click handler calls `open` directly when it is true (CouponScanner.kt:76-77), skipping the permission request. After the user revokes CAMERA in Settings the flag stays true, so `CameraManager.openCamera` is called without permission and throws SecurityException (CouponScanner.kt:44). Nothing clears the flag when the permission disappears.
Fix approach: Drop the SharedPreferences grant cache. Check the live permission at each tap with ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission(context, CAMERA) and only call open() when it returns GRANTED; otherwise launch the RequestPermission contract again. Put the permission check behind a small injectable function so the decision can be unit tested. Optionally wrap openCamera in try/catch SecurityException and surface an error status as a fallback.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:31-34 - the only camera-access state is a SharedPreferences boolean `camera_granted`, read by hasCameraAccess; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:36-38 - rememberCameraGranted writes true once and nothing ever writes false or re-checks the system permission; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:64-67 - the permission result callback sets the cached flag and opens the camera; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:76-77 - the Scan button opens the camera whenever the cached flag is true, with no live permission check; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt:41-44 - open() calls cameras.openCamera with @SuppressLint("MissingPermission"), so a revoked permission throws SecurityException here; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:74 - the checkout form hosts ScanCouponButton() with no permission handling of its own

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScanner.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM unit test, src/test/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CouponScannerDecisionTest.kt, that exercises the extracted decision function (for example `fun scanAction(hasPermission: () -> Boolean): ScanAction`, returning Open or RequestPermission). Test 1: when the permission checker returns true, the action is Open. Test 2: start with the checker returning true, then flip it to false to simulate revocation, and assert the action is RequestPermission and never Open. Before the fix there is no such decision point and the cached flag always yields Open, so the test fails. After the fix it passes.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I fixed the crash in `CouponScanner.kt`. The scan button no longer trusts a saved "camera granted" flag; it checks the live permission on every tap. The unit test compiles, but I haven't run it, and I haven't re-run the revoke attack on a device.

- **Permission check:** I removed the SharedPreferences cache. `hasCameraAccess` now calls `ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission`. A new `scanAction(hasPermission)` function returns `Open` or `RequestPermission`, and the click handler follows it. After a revoke, the next tap asks for permission again instead of opening the camera.
- **Fallback:** `open()` also catches `SecurityException` and shows the "Camera permission is needed to scan coupons" status.
- **Regression test:** The test class is `CouponScannerDecisionTest`. It checks that a granted permission gives `Open`. It also checks that flipping the checker to false after a granted call gives `RequestPermission`.
